name: Tenant Usage
description: Usage metric tracking per tenant (API calls, storage GB, seats). Source for plan-limit enforcement.
author: Kuray Karaaslan

erasure.note: monthly aggregate usage counters of the tenant

metadata.label: Usage threshold
metadata.description: A metered usage metric crossed an alert threshold (e.g. 80% / 95% of quota).

metadata.label: Usage overage
metadata.description: A metered usage metric exceeded its plan quota (overage billing trigger).

extensions.description: The usage counters projected as readings of kind tenant_usage (entity = the tenant; keys = the declared metrics; one row per minute window of summed increments), class 365, readable for the tenant's own entity with tenant_usage.metrics.read, shown to dashboards; quotas never read it (42-telemetry/06).

permissions.name: Read declared usage metrics and quotas

extensionPoints.description: Told that a tenant's use of a metered quota passed one of its alert thresholds this month (Usage settings; 80 and 95 % by default), used it up, or went over it (docs/phases/53-setting-levels 53.9, D173). tenant_usage sends the usage.threshold / usage.overage webhooks itself; a listener does what the tenant's people see: tenant_subscription tells the tenant's owners and points them to the usage packs. Default export: QuotaAlertListener { quotaAlert(alert: { tenantId, metric, label, quotaKey, used, limit, percent, kind: 'threshold' | 'exhausted' | 'overage', threshold?, month }) => Promise<void> } (server/tenant_usage.extension-points.ts). Fired from the periodic usage job, at most once per metric, kind and threshold a month; best-effort (a failing listener is logged). Platform gate: a quota is the platform's billing, owed whatever the tenant switched on.

A module declares a period metric it increments through TenantUsageService.increment/incrementBatch, without editing tenant_usage. The declaration is the contribution's static metadata: { label, unit, period: 'month' | 'day', quotaKey? } with the contribution key as the metric key (lowerCamel, stable forever); quotaKey names the feature_gate LIMIT it is enforced against (feature_gate.period-quota / tenant_usage.quota). The default export documents the same object; only the metadata is read, so no code loads on the hot path. The six original metrics are declared by tenant_usage itself and cannot be redefined. Undeclared keys are logged and dropped, never thrown.
